keyframe_review.note: 388,316 km2, the whole of modern Morocco, is too much: the page says the first Wattasid sultan held only the north, and the Saadians held Marrakesh from 1524 and the south by the Tadla partition of 1527 (Saadi Sultanate page). The infobox gives 'Established: 1472', so 1468-1471 is the Marinid-to-Wattasid transition: 'In 1465 [Abd al-Haqq II] was killed in a revolt in Fez, after which the Wattasids eventually established control over the former Marinid realm'. The shape holds from 1472, the dossier's start ('Established: 1472'); 1468-1471 is the sharifian interlude at Fez after the Marinid fall (marinid-sultanate dossier) and is not drawn as Wattasid (reviewer af-02-e). The page gives no area figure, so no infobox comparison is possible.

keyframe_review.note: 384,418 km2 for 1552-1555 is not supported: the Wattasids had no land from January 1549 to January 1554 (the pages name none; the Wattasid page says only that the last king was captured). In 1554 the Ottoman-backed Abu Hassun 'defeated the Saadians in January 1554' (Saadi page) and 'briefly retook Fez in 1554' (Wattasid page), until Muhammad al-Shaykh 'retook Fez in September 1554'. So Fez alone is Wattasid in 1554, nothing in 1552-1553 and 1555.

The Wattasid page gives other dates ('1548: the last Wattasid king is captured by the Saadians'; '1550: Saadians conquer Fez'); the Saadi page's day is followed. notes: Wattasid dynasty (af-02-e). (1) Cliopatria draws all of modern Morocco (384k km2) for 1468-1555; the page says the Wattasids held only the north (the south 'divided into several principalities') and the Treaty of Tadla (1527, Saadi page) split Morocco along the Oum Er-Rbia, so every shape is marked adjust to a north-only region; the infobox area is silent. (2) Dates: the page says Established 1472 (Cliopatria 1468; the Marinid dossier ends the Marinids in 1465, so 1466-1471 is a transition nobody owns; shape 1468 kept for 1468-1471 to avoid a hole). End: 1554 (Cliopatria 1555); the Saadi row starts 1556, so 1555 is Saadi in the Saadi dossier's new keyframe. The Wattasid page contradicts itself on the fall (1548 last king captured; 1550 Saadians conquer Fez; supplanted 1554); the Saadi page's 28 January 1549 is used for Fez. (3) Tangier and Asilah: Tangier page gives 28 August 1471 (Portugal), before the 1472 start, so no Wattasid loss event; the Marinid dossier records Tangier as 1465 from the Marinid page, a disagreement a gap-filler can settle. Asilah is named on the Tangier page without a year. (4) The southern Portuguese enclaves (Safi 1488, Mazagan 1502, Agadir 1505, from the Wattasid page's list) lie south of the Oum Er-Rbia, i.e. outside the corrected Wattasid land, so they are not Wattasid loss events; the Portuguese dossier (portuguese-africa) should carry them; the El Jadida page dates only a 1502 landing and a 1514 citadel. Azemmour (1513) and Santa Cruz: page silent. (5) Ottoman suzerainty from 1545 ('Vassal of the Ottoman Empire from 1545' in the infobox, a footnote says it was brief and Morocco 'remained largely independent'): vassal events belong in the Ottoman dossier (ottoman-empire, group me-10) with counterpart wattasid-dynasty; none is written here. (6) Pages silent: infobox area, Zayyanid relations, the Peñón de Vélez conquest itself. No Spanish Peñón loss is claimed beyond the page's 1508 date. (7) Names the gazetteer may lack: none beyond places used by radius.
